title: Psoriasis Comorbidity Screening & Baseline Workup
subtitle: History → Exam → Comorbidity screen → Labs → Vaccinations before systemic therapy

items.label: Duration and distribution of skin disease
items.detail: Onset age, body surface area trend, prior flares and triggers (stress, infection, medications, alcohol, smoking).

items.label: Joint symptoms: pain, stiffness, swelling
items.detail: Morning stiffness >30 min, DIP involvement, sausage digits (dactylitis), heel pain (enthesitis) — screen for PsA. Up to 30% of plaque psoriasis patients develop PsA.

items.label: GI symptoms: diarrhea, bloody stool, abdominal pain
items.detail: Screen for inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's, UC) — shared IL-17/IL-23 axis. Relevant to biologic selection (avoid IL-17 inhibitors in IBD).

items.label: Neurological history: numbness, weakness, visual changes
items.detail: Screen for demyelinating disease / MS. TNF-α inhibitors are contraindicated in demyelinating conditions.

items.label: Depression and anxiety screen (PHQ-9)
items.detail: Psoriasis patients have 2× higher prevalence of depression. PHQ-9 score ≥10 warrants referral. Treatment of psoriasis often improves mood.

items.label: Cardiovascular risk factors: smoking, hypertension, DM, obesity
items.detail: Psoriasis is an independent CV risk factor. Document BMI, smoking pack-years, HTN, DM, hyperlipidemia.

items.label: Alcohol use and quantity
items.detail: Heavy alcohol worsens psoriasis and is a relative contraindication to methotrexate. Use AUDIT-C screening tool.

items.label: Family history of psoriasis and PsA
Prior treatments: topicals, phototherapy, systemics, biologics
items.detail: Document reason for discontinuation (failure, intolerance, adverse event). Critical for therapy selection and payer requirements.

items.label: Medications: beta-blockers, lithium, NSAIDs, antimalarials
items.detail: These can trigger or worsen psoriasis flares.

items.label: BSA estimation (rule of nines or palm method)
items.detail: Patient palm = ~1% BSA. Assess all body regions systematically. Document percentage for PASI/severity classification.

items.label: PASI calculation (0–72 scale)
items.detail: Psoriasis Area and Severity Index: erythema + induration + scaling × area score for 4 regions. PASI >10 = moderate-severe; PASI 90 = treatment response target.

items.label: Nail exam: pitting, onycholysis, oil drop sign, subungual hyperkeratosis
items.detail: Nail psoriasis is associated with concurrent PsA. Nail pitting (>20 pits) and onycholysis are most specific. Document nail NAPSI score if severe.

items.label: Joint exam: DIP joints, dactylitis, enthesis (Achilles, plantar fascia, patella)
items.detail: Check for sausage digits (dactylitis), tender entheses, and DIP predominance. Order X-rays if PsA suspected (pencil-in-cup deformity).

items.label: Special site assessment: scalp, face, intertriginous, genitalia
items.detail: Scalp: assess with dermatoscope for adherent scale. Intertriginous: inverse psoriasis lacks scale. Genital psoriasis: highly impactful on QoL.

items.label: Metabolic syndrome screen: waist circumference, BP, BMI
items.detail: Psoriasis strongly associated with metabolic syndrome. Waist >102 cm (M) or >88 cm (F) + BP ≥130/85 + BMI ≥30 kg/m².

items.label: PsA screen: PEST questionnaire or PsAID-12
items.detail: Psoriasis Epidemiology Screening Tool (PEST): ≥3 points warrants rheumatology referral. Simple 5-question self-report. PsAID-12 for disease impact in known PsA.

items.label: DLQI (Dermatology Life Quality Index)
items.detail: 10-item validated QoL measure. DLQI 0-1 = no effect; DLQI >10 = very large effect on life. Used to classify severity and justify systemic therapy (NICE threshold: DLQI >10).

items.label: Metabolic syndrome and NAFLD screen
items.detail: Fasting glucose, lipid panel, LFTs, waist circumference. Fatty liver disease screen with LFTs before methotrexate; consider fibroscan if elevated.

items.label: PHQ-9 for depression
items.detail: Score ≥10 = moderate depression; ≥15 = moderately severe. Refer to mental health if positive. Biologic treatment can improve mood outcomes.

stages.name: Baseline Labs Before Biologic / Systemic Therapy

items.label: CBC with differential
items.detail: Rule out hematologic abnormalities. Monitor on methotrexate (cytopenia). Baseline for biologics.

items.label: CMP (comprehensive metabolic panel)
items.detail: Renal function (BUN/Cr) — essential before cyclosporine. Electrolytes. Glucose for metabolic syndrome.

items.label: LFTs (AST, ALT, alkaline phosphatase, albumin)
items.detail: Baseline hepatic function before methotrexate (hepatotoxic). Screen for NAFLD. Required for biologics.

items.label: Fasting lipid panel
items.detail: Assess cardiovascular risk. Cyclosporine can worsen dyslipidemia. Document baseline before biologic.

items.label: HBV serology (HBsAg, HBsAb, HBcAb)
items.detail: TNF-α inhibitors and IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors can reactivate HBV. If HBsAg+: consult hepatology; prophylactic antiviral therapy required. If HBcAb+ only: monitor LFTs closely.

items.label: HCV antibody
items.detail: If positive: confirm active infection with HCV RNA. Treat HCV before or in parallel with systemic psoriasis therapy.

items.label: HIV screen
items.detail: HIV can trigger or worsen psoriasis. Antiretroviral therapy may improve psoriasis. Required baseline before biologics.

items.label: Latent TB: QuantiFERON-TB Gold (preferred) or TST/PPD
items.detail: Mandatory before any biologic. If LTBI positive: complete 9 months INH prophylaxis (or 4 months rifampin) before starting TNF-α inhibitor; IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors may start earlier per guidelines. Chest X-ray if positive.

items.label: Pregnancy test if applicable
items.detail: Essential before methotrexate and acitretin (both teratogenic). Methotrexate requires contraception during and 3 months after use. Acitretin requires contraception for 3 years after.

items.label: ANA if systemic lupus/connective tissue disease suspected
LIVE vaccines must be given BEFORE biologic initiation
items.detail: Live attenuated vaccines (varicella/zoster, MMR, yellow fever, live flu nasal spray) are CONTRAINDICATED while on biologics or immunosuppressants. Administer ≥4 weeks before starting biologic.

items.label: Zoster vaccine (Shingrix — recombinant, non-live)
items.detail: Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV/Shingrix) is preferred over live Zostavax. Can be given before OR after biologic initiation. Recommended for patients ≥50 years or immunosuppressed.

items.label: Influenza vaccine (annual, inactivated)
items.detail: Annual inactivated flu vaccine recommended. Live-attenuated nasal spray is contraindicated on biologics.

items.label: Pneumococcal vaccines (PCV20 or PCV15 + PPSV23)
items.detail: PCV20 alone or PCV15 followed by PPSV23 ≥1 year later. Important for all patients on systemic immunosuppression.

items.label: COVID-19 and other routine vaccinations
items.detail: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines are safe and effective during biologic therapy. Update Tdap, hepatitis A/B if not immune.

citations.quote: Elmets CA et al. Joint AAD-NPF guidelines of care for psoriasis with awareness and attention to comorbidities. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2019.
